problem: A hair straightener reaches a temperature of ${450}^{∘}\text{F}.$ After turning it off, the temperature $T(t)$ of the straightener decreases at a rate that obeys Newton's law of cooling. Here, $T$ is measured in degrees Fahrenheit, and $t>0$ is the time in minutes. If the room temperature is ${75}^{∘}\text{F},$ which differential equation could be used to model the straightener temperature? Assume that $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.
worked_solution:
Newton's law of cooling states that the rate at which the temperature $T(t)$ of a body changes is proportional to the difference between its temperature and its surroundings. Therefore, we have the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=-k(T-{T}_{S}),
$$

where ${T}_{S}$ is the temperature of the surroundings, and $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

In our case, ${T}_{S}={75}^{∘}\text{F},$ and we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}T}{\text{d}t}=-k(T-75).
$$
